title: Tomato leaf curl virus management
text: The disease is spread by whiteflies. Remove infected plants early, use yellow sticky traps, and control whiteflies with neem-based products or recommended insecticides. Fungicides do not cure viral disease.

title: Early and late blight in tomato
text: Avoid overhead irrigation and remove infected leaves. Use recommended protectant fungicides such as mancozeb, and systemic combinations for late blight, at first symptoms.

title: Tomato fruit borer
text: Install pheromone traps, collect and destroy damaged fruits, and use Bt or NPV based biopesticides at early larval stages.

title: Pink bollworm management
text: Use pheromone traps to monitor moths, destroy damaged bolls and crop residue, and avoid late-season excess nitrogen that prolongs the crop.

title: Sucking pests (whitefly, aphid, jassid)
text: Use yellow sticky traps, spray neem-based products early, manage weeds, and avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays that kill natural enemies.

title: Rice blast management
text: Avoid excess nitrogen, use resistant varieties, and apply recommended fungicide such as tricyclazole at early symptom stage.

title: Brown planthopper
text: Avoid heavy nitrogen, maintain wider spacing, drain the field and spray only on the plant base when threshold is crossed.

title: Yellow stem borer
text: Use pheromone traps, release Trichogramma egg parasitoids, and remove egg masses in the nursery.
